prompt: An aromatic hydrocarbon shows M⁺ at 92 and a huge peak at m/z = 91 (loss of 1 H). What is going on?

options.label: Toluene → benzyl cation → aromatic tropylium (C₇H₇⁺, m/z 91) — super stable, dominant peak

explanation: Toluene (M=92) loses H to give the benzyl cation (C₆H₅-CH₂⁺) which rapidly rearranges to the TROPYLIUM cation — a 7-membered aromatic ring with 6 π electrons (Hückel). Super stable → m/z=91 is often the base peak. Diagnostic for alkylbenzenes.
